title: Enum singletons and ordered enum sets

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, in which situation is an enum singleton the wrong choice?

options.text: When the singleton has to extend some other class
options.says: The page lists needing to extend another class among the cases against an enum singleton, because every enum already extends Enum.

options.text: When the singleton has to survive serialization
options.says: The page names serialization safety as an advantage: deserialization always returns the same instance.

options.text: When the singleton is shared by many threads
options.says: The page names thread safety as an advantage: the JVM guarantees a single instantiation during class loading.

origin.section: Q4: When should you use enum singletons vs. other singleton patterns?

questions.stem: Per this page, can Java 21 code call `getFirst()` or `reversed()` on an `EnumSet`?

options.text: Yes, because Java 21 made every JDK set that has an order a SequencedSet
options.says: The page says EnumSet is the exception here: in Java 21 it does not implement SequencedSet.

options.text: Yes, but only for enums of at most 64 constants, held in a RegularEnumSet
options.says: The page makes no exception by size: EnumSet as such does not implement SequencedSet in Java 21.

options.text: No, because EnumSet keeps declaration order yet is not a SequencedSet
options.says: The page says EnumSet iterates in declaration order but does not implement SequencedSet in Java 21, so copy it into a List or use a TreeSet for those methods.

concepts: Enum singletons are thread-safe, serialization-safe and reflection-proof, but do not fit when the singleton must extend a class, load lazily or be replaced in tests.
EnumSet iterates in declaration order but does not implement SequencedSet in Java 21.
